extraction_metadata.extraction_notes: Marks derived mechanically: column boundaries and row bands recovered from 200 dpi raster rule lines (the row bands read from the Comment column, never from a redacted label cell), text-layer tokens assigned to the resulting cells, and the whole matrix cross-checked with a near-black-pixel count (<90) per cell rectangle. The two methods agreed on every cell of all nine pages. Column positions 2-21 are the union of the two tiles; marks were unioned by activity name across tiles.

table_metadata.table_title: Table 2. Schedule of Activities for the Maintenance Treatment Period of Study J1P-MC-KFAH
table_metadata.table_purpose: Maintenance Treatment Period schedule (V10-V29, weeks 14-52, study days 99-365) for participants who are responders at Week 12.
table_metadata.notes: TABLE TYPE (as fixed by the boundary agent, and independently supported here): 'track', track_label 'Responders'. The population sentence 'This schedule applies to study participants who are responders at Week 12.' is printed under the title on all nine pages of this table; Table 3 prints the mirror sentence for nonresponders, so the two tables schedule mutually exclusive populations even though their visit labels, weeks and study days are numerically identical. No disagreement with the agreed structure. TILED: this is ONE logical table printed as two side-by-side column-block tiles - tile A = V10-V19 (doc 24-27, title 'Table 2. Schedule of Activities for the Maintenance Treatment Period of Study J1P-MC-KFAH'), tile B = V20-V29 (doc 28-32, title 'Table 2 (continued). Schedule of activities for the Maintenance Treatment Period of Study J1P-MC-KFAH', lowercase 'activities'). COLUMNS: L=1 leading label column, so the first data column is position 2. The two tiles are unioned into 20 data columns: positions 2-11 = V10-V19, positions 12-21 = V20-V29. The right-hand 'Comment' column is a notes column, not a schedule column and not an activity (prompt section 6); its cells are emitted as footnote annotations, so it occupies no column_position. (The agreed structure said 'Comment' is position 11 in Tables 1-3 tiles; with L=1 and 10 data columns per tile that arithmetic would give 12 for a single tile of this table, and in the unioned 20-column model the notes column has no position at all. Recorded here rather than silently.) ROW UNION ACROSS TILES: 33 of the 40 body rows print in BOTH tiles and their marks were unioned by activity name. Seven rows print in only one tile: Review modified Mayo score (MMS), Diary return, Clinician-Administered Questionnaires (Paper), Physician's Global Assessment (PGA), Endoscopy, and Colon biopsy sample collection are tile-B only; the tile-A header block explains the endoscopy absence in the Comment column of the Endoscopic Procedure row - 'Not applicable for responders during the time period of V10 through V19'. PAGE COVERAGE (declared section 4 tiled exception): doc pages 30 and 32 contribute no activity rows because every row printed there also prints in tile A and was first read there. Doc 30 supplied the V21-V29 marks for Hematology, Clinical chemistry, Lipid panel, Urinalysis, Urine pregnancy (local), the CCI row between them and HBV DNA; doc 32 supplied the V20-V28 Dosing marks and the 'No dosing at V29.' note. REDACTIONS: eight body rows are redacted to a black bar labelled 'CCI' and still carry marks - they are transcribed as activity_name 'CCI' and never repaired. Under 'Stool Samples' a single two-row-tall CCI bar covers TWO activity rows (row_position 42 and 43): the 'CCI' glyph is drawn in the upper row in the tile-A print (doc 27) and in the lower row in the tile-B print (doc 31), so row 43's name is recorded with method 'visual_transcription'. Both rows carry X at V15, V21 and V29. GLYPH-SPREAD TEXT LAYER: doc pages 24, 26, 27, 28, 30, 31 come back letter-spaced ('S c h e d ul e of A cti viti es'); doc 25, 29 and 32 are clean. Activity names and annotation text from the spread pages were rebuilt by word re-segmentation and verified against a 200 dpi render, and carry method provenance. HEADER-BLOCK WORDING DIFFERS BETWEEN TILES and is transcribed as printed, not harmonised: tile A prints 'For procedures at an ETV, see ETV in Table 4.' and '...or a combination thereof), if written approval...'; tile B prints 'For procedures at an early termination visit, see ETV in Table 4.' and '...or a combination thereof) if written approval...' (no comma). Both variants are kept as separate annotations (h2/h3, h5/h6). 'Fasting visit' is transcribed as a schedule_property, not an activity - see its property_comment. The Comment cell on HBV DNA prints 'anti‑HBc' with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011) while the abbreviations block on doc 32 prints 'anti-HBc' with an ASCII hyphen; both are transcribed as printed. Multi-line activity labels are wrapped differently between the two tiles, so activity_name_source.cell_text carries the label as one line; no row has leading whitespace in the text layer (every label starts at x=77.28 pt), so hierarchy is taken from the bold + grey shading of the section-header bands (indentation_method font_signal). The abbreviations block on doc 32 yields no annotations: none of its terms is printed as a marker in a grid cell, header cell or activity label (prompt section 6).

schedule_properties.property_comment: Visit identifiers V10 through V29 across the two horizontally tiled column blocks of this table (tile A prints V10-V19, the '(continued)' tile B prints V20-V29). Values are named visits, hence property_type 'visit'; it is the topmost header row, hence hierarchical_level 1.
Week number counted from randomization (14, 16, ... 52, every 2 weeks). Numeric week offsets, hence property_type 'week'; second header row under Visit number.
Protocol study day for each visit (99, 113, ... 365, 14-day spacing). Protocol day numbers, hence property_type 'study_day'; third header row.

Permitted visit window, printed as ±3 for every one of the 20 visits. A visit window, hence property_type 'window'; fourth header row. The value is identical in every column, so it does not by itself distinguish columns, but it carries per-column data and is part of the stacked header block.

Grey-shaded, bold band printed immediately below the four header rows on EVERY page of both tiles (doc pages 24-32), marking which visits are fasting visits: X at V15 (tile A) and at V29 (tile B). It is a qualifier band on the visit columns rather than a procedure performed on a participant, and it reprints with the header block on the last page (doc 32) which carries only the Randomization and Dosing rows - so it is transcribed as a schedule_property, not an activity. hierarchical_level null: it qualifies columns already distinguished by Visit number.

annotations.annotation_text: This schedule applies to study participants who are responders at Week 12.
For procedures at an ETV, see ETV in Table 4.
For procedures at an early termination visit, see ETV in Table 4.
For procedures at an unscheduled visit, see V997 in Table 4.

Visits 10 through 28 are eligible to be conducted remotely (that is, by telephone, IT-assisted virtual visit, mobile healthcare, or a combination thereof), if written approval is provided by the sponsor and according to the preferences of the participant and the study site. However, no more than 34 days can elapse without an on-site study visit occurring.

Visits 10 through 28 are eligible to be conducted remotely (that is, by telephone, IT-assisted virtual visit, mobile healthcare, or a combination thereof) if written approval is provided by the sponsor and according to the preferences of the participant and the study site. However, no more than 34 days can elapse without an on-site study visit occurring.
For AESIs, additional data are collected (Section 8.3.6).
